title: Ethiopian Spiced Beef Ribs
community: All of Ethiopia — the rib stew of celebration
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Godn Wat — beef short ribs slow-cooked in a Key Wat-style berbere sauce for 2 hours until the meat is falling off the bone and the bone marrow has enriched the sauce. The rib version of the celebration wat — the most gelatinous and richest of all the beef wats.
longDesc: Beef rib wat is made for special occasions when the bones are as important as the meat — the marrow and collagen from the ribs create the richest, most deeply flavoured berbere sauce of any Ethiopian wat. Served with the ribs still in the sauce, to be eaten bone-in.
ingredients: 1.2 kg beef short ribs — cut between the bones
steps: Add kibbeh and berbere. Toast 4 minutes.
The meat should fall off the bone. Sauce should be very thick.
chefTips: 2 hours minimum — the ribs release their collagen slowly.
The marrow enriches the sauce — do not remove the bones.
cookingScience: Beef short ribs contain a high proportion of collagen and bone marrow. The marrow (primarily fat and stem cells) dissolves into the sauce at 90°C, enriching it significantly. The collagen converts to gelatin over 2 hours, producing the characteristically thick, coating sauce.
sustainabilityTips: Ribs are a secondary cut — excellent use of the whole animal.
culturalNote: Beef rib wat is the wat that Ethiopians make when they want to feed their guests from their very best — the ribs are expensive, the preparation is long, and the result is the most luxurious of all Ethiopian beef dishes.
